unit.title: Develop and monitor financial policy statements and operating procedures

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a financial policy statement in an organisation?
options: To record each day's financial transactions in detail
To set the rules and principles for handling money and assets
To replace the annual budget with a fixed set of figures for every year
To list the salaries of the finance staff for the year

questions.stem: Which statement best shows the difference between a financial policy and an operating procedure?
options: A policy is written for managers only; a procedure is written only for the auditors
A policy is written once; a procedure changes every single week
A policy says what must be done and why; a procedure says how, step by step
A policy covers income only; a procedure covers spending only

questions.stem: Which sentence belongs in an operating procedure rather than in the policy statement?
options: The company will pay only for travel that is needed for its business.
All spending must give value for money and be properly approved.
Staff must not gain personally from any purchase they arrange.
Attach the original receipts and submit the claim form within 30 days.

questions.stem: A growing Kingston distributor has no written credit policy, and its bad debts have doubled in two years. What is the best first step for the finance manager?
options: Analyse the debts and risks and the gaps in present practice
Copy the credit policy of a large bank and issue it the same week
Stop giving credit to every customer from tomorrow
Ask the sales team to write the policy without finance

questions.stem: Which is the strongest reason for a hotel to review and update its cash-handling policy now?
options: The policy is printed in an old font that staff dislike
The external auditor reported a weakness in cash controls
The finance manager wants a longer policy than last year's
A competitor recently changed the layout of its own policy

questions.stem: When drafting financial policies for a company, which outside requirement must the writer check first?
options: The policies the writer used at a previous employer in the same trade
The preferences of the firm's largest customer
Company law, tax law and other rules that apply to the firm
The style guide used by the firm's advertising agency

questions.stem: A public body is drafting its own procurement procedure. What must the procedure do?
options: Set rules that are looser than the national public procurement rules
Leave out the national rules, as each body may choose its own
Apply only to contracts that its chief executive chooses
Work within the national public procurement rules and add local detail

questions.stem: A policy on keeping financial records says invoices may be thrown away after one year. What is the main problem?
options: Records must be kept for the period tax and company law require
Invoices must be kept for ever, and only in their original paper form
Records may never be stored in electronic form at all
Only the auditor may decide to keep or destroy records

questions.stem: Andrea Morgan is drafting a new purchasing procedure for a school. Whom should she consult?
options: Only the principal, as the person who will approve it
The staff who buy, approve, receive and pay, and the auditors
Only the suppliers who sell to the school most often and know its needs
No one, so that the procedure is finished more quickly

questions.stem: Why should front-line staff be consulted on a draft operating procedure?
options: Because they must approve every policy before the board does
Because consultation with staff removes the need for any training later
Because they know where the steps will work or break in practice
Because the law requires every employee to sign each procedure

questions.stem: Which heading is most important near the start of a financial policy statement?
options: A list of the finance staff's qualifications
The history of the finance department
Thanks to everyone who helped with the draft
Purpose and scope: what and whom the policy covers

questions.stem: A draft travel policy says 'reasonable meal costs will be paid'. Staff at a Montego Bay firm read it in different ways. What should the writer do?
options: State a clear limit or rate per meal, and how to claim it
Leave it, so each manager can decide case by case
Remove meal costs from the policy altogether
Add the word 'very' before 'reasonable' to make it stricter

questions.stem: Why should a financial policy name the roles responsible for each part, such as 'budget holder' or 'finance manager', rather than people's names?
options: Because people's names are private and may not be printed
Because the policy stays valid when people change jobs
Because auditors are not allowed to know staff names
Because job titles are shorter to write than names

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a definitions section in a financial policy?
options: To make the policy longer and more formal
To translate the policy into another language
To make sure key terms are read in one way only
To list the words the writer found difficult

questions.stem: Which format usually makes an operating procedure easiest to follow?
options: Long paragraphs in formal legal language
A single sentence that sums up the whole process
A copy of the policy statement with the word 'procedure' added
Numbered steps, with who does each and the forms used

questions.stem: Kemar Lewis wants new accounts clerks to see the whole payment process at a glance. What should he add to the procedure?
options: A flowchart of the steps and decisions
A list of last year's payments
The finance manager's phone number
A copy of the company's annual report

questions.stem: A fixed asset policy says items costing J$100,000 or more are recorded as assets; cheaper items are charged as expenses. A printer costs J$85,000. How is it treated?
options: As a fixed asset, because it will last several years and is equipment
As an expense, because it is below the J$100,000 threshold
As a fixed asset, because all equipment is an asset
As an expense only if the manager agrees in writing

questions.stem: A firm sells on 30-day credit terms. Its debtors are J$3,600,000 and its credit sales are J$21,900,000 a year (use 365 days). What are its debtor days, and what do they show?
options: 30 days, so customers are paying exactly on terms
45 days, so customers are slightly slower than terms
60 days, so customers take twice the agreed time
120 days, so most debts should be written off now

questions.stem: A credit policy is being written for a building supplies firm in May Pen. Which item should it include?
options: A promise to give credit to any customer who asks
A rule that each salesperson sets the credit limits for their own customers
A ban on chasing any customer for late payment
Credit checks, limits, terms and steps for overdue accounts

questions.stem: A non-profit's reserves policy says it will hold cash equal to three months of operating costs. Yearly operating costs are J$48,000,000. What reserve does the policy require?
A travel policy pays J$60 per kilometre for staff who use their own cars on approved business. A return trip from Kingston is 180 km. What is the claim?
A firm buys supplies priced in US dollars. Which point belongs in its financial policies?
options: Staff may choose any exchange rate they like when recording costs
All US dollar costs must be left out of the accounts
How exchange rates are chosen and the currency risk is managed
Only cash may be used to pay overseas suppliers

questions.stem: An organisation's investment policy for spare cash should mainly set out what?
options: Which staff may invest their own savings through the firm
How to invest only in the highest-return shares available
Why spare cash should be kept in the office safe
The aims, approved types of investment, limits and who decides

questions.stem: Who should normally approve a new financial policy for a company?
options: The board, or a board committee with that power
The accounts clerk who drafted the operating procedure
The firm's largest supplier
Each staff member, by a show of hands

questions.stem: Before a draft policy goes to the board, what should the finance manager do?
options: Send it to all customers for comment
Check it against law, other policies and the systems in use
Print it and post it on the staff noticeboard as the final version
Ask the board to approve it without reading it

questions.stem: Two versions of the expense policy are in use in different branches. What would most help prevent this?
options: Printing the policy in a different colour each year
Letting each branch keep whichever version its staff like the best
Version control: a number, date, owner and one central copy
Sending the policy only to branch managers by post

questions.stem: A new procurement procedure has been approved at a parish council. What is the best way to put it into practice?
options: Email it once and assume everyone has read it
File it in the finance office until someone asks to see a copy of it
Wait until the first breach, then explain the rules
Brief and train the staff who use it, with guides and a contact

questions.stem: Why should staff confirm in writing that they have read and understood a key financial policy?
options: It gives a record that they were told, which supports later action
It makes the policy legally binding on all customers and suppliers too
It removes the need for managers to monitor compliance
It allows staff to change parts they do not like

questions.stem: A new expense policy needs a new claim form in the accounting system. When should the policy start?
options: The day it is approved, whether the form is ready or not
When the system, forms and training are ready
Only after the next external audit has finished
When each manager decides it suits their team

questions.stem: Which method gives a finance manager the best evidence that an expense policy is being followed?
options: Asking managers at their monthly meeting whether staff follow it
Waiting for complaints from staff about the policy
Testing a sample of claims against the policy each quarter
Counting the number of pages in the policy

questions.stem: A sample of 120 expense claims finds 18 that break the policy. What is the compliance rate?
Each month the system lists all payments made without a purchase order. What is this kind of monitoring report called?
options: An exception report
A cash budget
A trial balance
A strategic plan

questions.stem: Which measure best shows whether a new credit policy is working at a Mandeville wholesaler?
options: The number of pages in the credit application form
Debtor days and bad debts, compared before and after
The number of new customers the sales team visits
How many staff attended the launch briefing

questions.stem: Tests show that one branch breaks the purchasing procedure far more often than others. What should the manager do first?
options: Close the branch's purchasing account at once
Discipline every member of staff at the branch
Find out why: training, workload, system or a weak step
Change the procedure for all the branches so that it suits that one branch

questions.stem: What role does internal audit usually play in relation to financial policies?
options: It writes every procedure and runs the finance office
It approves each payment before it is made
It sets the organisation's prices and budgets
It gives an independent view of whether they are followed and work

questions.stem: A manager approves her own expense claim, which the policy forbids. The amount is small. What should happen?
options: The breach is reported and dealt with under the policy, whatever the amount
Nothing, because the amount is small
The claim is paid and the policy is changed so that it allows this in future
Her staff are told to approve her claims in future without checking

questions.stem: Staff keep breaking a procedure because one step takes three days and holds up urgent orders. What does this suggest?
options: The staff should be dismissed for breaking it, whatever the reason
The procedure itself may need to be reviewed and improved
The step should be kept and the orders delayed
Urgent orders should be banned at the firm

questions.stem: When should financial policies and procedures be reviewed?
options: Only when the auditors ask for a new copy
Only when a new finance manager starts
On a set cycle, and also when laws, systems or risks change
Never, once they have been approved by the board and printed for staff

questions.stem: A firm moves from paper invoices to an online accounting system. What must happen to its payment procedure?
options: Nothing, because the policy has not changed
It should be withdrawn and not replaced
Staff should keep the paper steps alongside the new system
It should be updated to match the new system and its controls

questions.stem: A new gifts and hospitality rule in the purchasing procedure contradicts the staff code of conduct. What should be done?
options: Agree one rule with HR and update both documents to match
Let staff choose which document to follow
Keep both as they are, as each covers a different department's staff
Remove the rule from both documents

questions.stem: Why should financial policies include a schedule of who may approve what, and up to which amount?
options: To show which staff earn the highest salaries
To make clear who has authority, so approvals are valid
To allow anyone to approve any amount at all in an emergency
To let the auditors approve large payments

questions.stem: Where should the current approved financial policies be kept?
options: On the finance manager's personal laptop only
In printed copies handed out once, years ago
In one central, controlled place that staff can reach
In each staff member's own email folders

questions.stem: How do financial policies in a ministry differ most from those in a private firm?
options: They need not follow any national law
They are set only by the private auditors
They may ignore value for money
They work within public finance and procurement rules

questions.stem: Six months after a new expense policy, claims are processed faster but staff complain about one rule. What is the best next step?
options: Review that rule with staff and evidence, and propose a change if needed
Withdraw the whole policy at once and go back to the old way of claiming
Ignore the complaints, as processing is faster
Tell staff that complaints about policies are not allowed

questions.stem: What most helps staff follow financial policies willingly rather than only out of fear?
options: Making the policies as long and as detailed as they can possibly be
Clear reasons for each rule and managers who follow them too
Keeping the policies secret from junior staff
Punishing every small breach heavily in public

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What two-word term names the step-by-step instructions that put a financial policy into practice?
What two-word term names a report that lists only the items that break a rule or limit, such as payments without a purchase order?
A test of 300 claims finds 36 submitted after the policy's 30-day limit. What percentage were late?
Debtors are J$1,500,000 and credit sales are J$18,250,000 a year. Using 365 days, what are the debtor days?
In a fixed asset policy, what is the cost level called above which an item is recorded as an asset? (One word, often with 'capitalisation' before it.)
What two-word term names the practice of numbering and dating each issue of a policy so that only the current one is used?
What term names the table that sets out which roles may approve which transactions, and up to what amount? (Three or four words.)
A reserves policy requires two months of operating costs. Yearly operating costs are J$30,000,000. What reserve is required, in J$?
What is the diagram called that shows the steps and decisions of a procedure with boxes and arrows?
Which function gives the board an independent view of whether financial policies are followed? (Two words.)
A policy pays J$4,500 a day for meals on approved travel. A trip lasts 4 days. What is the meal allowance, in J$?
A sample of 80 purchase orders finds 72 correctly approved. What is the compliance rate?
What three-word phrase names the aim of getting the best mix of cost, quality and results from spending?
Which body in a company normally gives final approval to its main financial policies? (One or two words.)
What is the protected channel called through which staff can report suspected breaches without fear of reprisal? (One word, often followed by 'policy'.)

essays.stem: Describe the steps you would follow to develop a new financial policy, from identifying the need to its approval by the board.
essays.modelAnswer: I would begin by defining the need: the risk, audit finding, legal change or growth that makes a policy necessary, and what the policy must achieve. Next I would research the requirements: company and tax law, any sector or public finance rules, and our existing policies, so the new one fits. I would map present practice to see where it falls short. I would then draft the policy in a set format: purpose, scope, definitions, policy statements, roles and responsibilities, links to procedures, monitoring and review date. I would consult the people affected, such as budget holders, finance staff, HR and internal audit, and test the draft against real cases. After revising it, I would check it against our systems and the delegation of authority, and prepare a short paper for the board or finance committee explaining the need, the main rules, the costs of putting it in place and the plan for training. Once approved, it would be issued under version control.
markingPoints: Defines the need and the purpose of the policy
Researches legal and organisational requirements and present practice
Drafts in a clear format with scope, roles and review date
Consults the people affected and tests the draft
Prepares the case for board approval and issues under version control

essays.stem: Compare a financial policy statement with an operating procedure, using the example of staff expense claims. Explain why an organisation needs both.
essays.modelAnswer: A policy statement sets out the principles and rules and the reasons for them. For expenses, it might say that the firm repays only reasonable costs incurred for its business, sets limits for meals and hotels, requires receipts, forbids staff from approving their own claims and says breaches will be dealt with under the disciplinary rules. It is approved by the board and changes rarely. An operating procedure explains how the policy is carried out, step by step: which form or screen to use, what to attach, who checks the claim, how it is approved, how finance pays it, and the time limits at each stage. It is owned by management and is updated when the system or forms change. An organisation needs both because the policy gives authority, consistency and a basis for decisions, while the procedure lets staff apply it correctly every day. A policy without a procedure is applied in different ways; a procedure without a policy has no clear authority behind it.
markingPoints: Explains the policy as principles, rules and reasons, approved at board level
Explains the procedure as practical steps, roles, forms and timings
Uses the expense claim example for both
Notes different owners and frequency of change
Justifies why both are needed and the risk of having only one

essays.stem: A wholesaler sells on 30-day terms. Its debtors are J$3,600,000 and credit sales are J$21,900,000 a year, and bad debts have doubled. Work out its debtor days and recommend what its new credit policy should contain.
essays.modelAnswer: Credit sales per day are J$21,900,000 ÷ 365 = J$60,000. Debtor days are J$3,600,000 ÷ J$60,000 = 60 days, so customers take on average twice the agreed 30 days. This ties up cash and helps explain the rise in bad debts. The new policy should set out who may be given credit and how: an application form, trade and bank references and a check of the customer's history. It should set credit limits by customer, approved at levels shown in the delegation of authority, and standard terms of 30 days, stated on every invoice. It should set the collection steps: a statement at month end, a reminder at 7 days overdue, a call at 14 days, stopping supply at 30 days and referral for recovery after that, with the approval needed to write off a debt. It should require a monthly aged debtors report to management and a target for debtor days, such as 40 days within a year, so that results can be monitored.
markingPoints: Credit sales per day J$60,000 and debtor days 60 correct
Interprets the result against 30-day terms and the cash and bad-debt effect
Includes credit checks and approved credit limits
Includes clear terms and timed collection steps, with write-off approval
Includes monitoring: aged debtors report and a debtor-days target

essays.stem: A new procurement policy and procedure have been approved for a public agency with offices in four parishes. Plan how you would put them into practice.
essays.modelAnswer: I would set a start date that allows time for the system changes, forms and training to be ready, and publish the documents in one central place with version numbers. I would brief the senior team first so that they lead by example, then hold short training sessions in each office for staff who request, approve, receive and pay, using real examples and the new forms. I would produce a one-page quick guide and a flowchart, name a contact officer for questions, and ask staff to confirm in writing that they have read the documents. For the first two months I would run a help desk and review early transactions closely, giving feedback rather than blame for honest errors. I would agree measures, such as the share of purchases with approved orders, and report them monthly. After three months I would collect feedback from each office and fix unclear steps. Throughout, the procedure must stay within the national public procurement rules.
markingPoints: Realistic start date with systems, forms and a central controlled copy
Leaders briefed first and targeted training for each role and office
Quick guides, a contact person and written confirmation by staff
Close early monitoring with supportive feedback and measures
Review after an early period, fixing unclear steps, within national rules

essays.stem: Explain how you would monitor whether staff follow the organisation's financial policies and procedures, and what you would do with the results.
essays.modelAnswer: I would set clear measures for each key policy, such as the share of expense claims with receipts, payments with approved orders, and debtor days. I would use system exception reports each month, such as payments without orders or claims over limits, and test a sample of transactions each quarter against the policy, recording the compliance rate. I would ask budget holders to confirm compliance in their areas and use internal audit's findings. Staff feedback and complaints also show where rules are unclear. I would report results to management and the finance or audit committee, with trends over time. Where I find breaches, I would first find the cause: lack of training, a step that does not work, workload or deliberate abuse. Training, clearer guidance or a change to the procedure fixes most problems; deliberate or repeated breaches are dealt with under the disciplinary rules. I would track actions until closed, and use the evidence in the next policy review.
markingPoints: Sets measures for key policies
Uses exception reports and sample testing, with a compliance rate
Uses budget holders, internal audit and staff feedback
Reports results with trends to management or a committee
Finds causes and acts proportionately, tracking actions and feeding the review

essays.stem: Your organisation's financial policies were written eight years ago and have not been reviewed. Plan a review and justify each step.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would list every financial policy and procedure, with its owner and date, because we cannot review what we have not found. Second, I would check each against current law, public or sector rules and our present systems, since eight years of change in tax rules, technology and the organisation make gaps likely. Third, I would gather evidence on how well each works: audit findings, exception reports, compliance tests, losses and staff feedback. This shows which policies are risky or ignored. Fourth, I would rank the policies by risk and agree a timetable with the finance committee, so that high-risk areas such as payments and cash come first. Fifth, owners would redraft, consulting the users, removing contradictions and adding version control and review dates. Sixth, the revised policies go for approval, with training and communication. Finally, I would set a review cycle, such as every two or three years, or sooner when laws, systems or risks change, so the problem does not return.
markingPoints: Lists all policies with owners and dates
Checks against current law, rules and systems
Gathers evidence of how each works (audit, exceptions, feedback)
Ranks by risk and agrees a timetable; redrafts with consultation
Approval, training and a set review cycle, each step justified

essays.stem: A test of expense claims at a hotel finds that 18 of 120 claims broke the policy: most lacked receipts, and two were approved by the claimant. Evaluate the findings and recommend action.
essays.modelAnswer: Eighteen of 120 is 15% non-compliance, so the compliance rate is 85%. That is too low for a basic control, and it shows the policy is not well understood or not enforced. Most of the breaches, missing receipts, suggest a training or process problem: staff may not know the rule, or the form may let them submit without receipts. These can be fixed by retraining, a clearer form and a system rule that blocks claims with no attachment. The two self-approved claims are more serious, because they break a key control and could hide fraud. I would check whether the amounts were genuine, report them to the general manager and deal with them under the policy and the disciplinary rules, while asking why the system allowed it. I would then block self-approval in the system, remind all approvers of their duty, and retest a new sample in three months, aiming for at least 95% compliance. I would report the results to the finance committee.
markingPoints: Works out 15% non-compliance or 85% compliance and judges it
Separates minor process errors from the serious self-approval breach
Recommends training, clearer forms and system controls for receipts
Investigates and acts on the self-approvals under the policy, and blocks them in the system
Plans a retest with a target and reports to management or a committee

essays.stem: Explain what makes a financial policy statement clear, usable and enforceable. Give examples of good and poor wording.
essays.modelAnswer: A clear policy has a stated purpose and scope, so readers know why it exists and whom it covers. It uses plain language, short sentences and defined terms. Poor wording such as 'reasonable costs will normally be met' leaves too much to judgement; good wording such as 'hotel costs are repaid up to the rate in Schedule A, with an itemised receipt' can be applied the same way every time. Using 'must' for rules and 'should' for good practice shows what is required. Roles are named by job title, for example 'the budget holder approves claims for their cost centre; no one may approve their own claim'. It links to the operating procedure and forms. To be enforceable, it must be approved by the right body, communicated and acknowledged by staff, and say what happens in a breach. It should fit the law and other policies, carry a version number and review date, and be kept in one controlled place.
markingPoints: Purpose, scope and defined terms
Plain, precise wording, with a good and a poor example
Clear use of 'must' and named roles
Links to procedures and states consequences of breaches
Approved, communicated, consistent with law and other policies, under version control

essays.stem: Compare developing financial policies for a ministry with developing them for a private company.
essays.modelAnswer: In both, policies set rules for handling money and assets, need consultation and clear drafting, and must be monitored and reviewed. The differences are in authority, purpose and accountability. A company's policies are approved by its board and must follow company and tax law, but within those it has wide freedom to set its own rules to protect shareholders' interests. A ministry works within national public finance and procurement rules, Finance Ministry instructions and the budget voted by Parliament, so its policies mostly add local detail and cannot be looser than those rules. Its purpose is value for money for the public rather than profit, and its accountability runs to the Permanent Secretary, the Auditor General and Parliament, so records and audit trails must be especially complete. Public bodies may also have to explain decisions under access to information rules. Changes can be slower because more approvals are needed. A private firm can change faster, but must still answer to its board and auditors.
markingPoints: Similarities: rules for money, consultation, drafting, monitoring and review
Company: board approval, company and tax law, wider freedom
Ministry: works within national public finance and procurement rules
Different purpose and accountability lines (public value, auditors, Parliament)
Practical effects: records, transparency and speed of change

essays.stem: Justify why senior managers' behaviour matters for compliance with financial policies, and recommend how a finance manager can build a culture of compliance.
essays.modelAnswer: Staff watch what leaders do more than what policies say. If a director skips approvals to 'get things done', claims expenses outside the rules or ignores audit findings, staff learn that the rules are optional, and breaches spread. If leaders follow the same rules, explain them and act on breaches fairly, staff see the policies as part of how the organisation works. So senior behaviour largely decides whether policies work. A finance manager can build a culture of compliance by writing policies that are clear and practical, with the reasons stated, and by consulting users so the rules make sense. She can ask the chief executive and directors to brief their teams and to follow the rules visibly. Training should be regular, with quick guides and an easy contact for questions. She should report compliance results openly, praise teams that improve, and fix procedures that cause breaches. Breaches should be handled consistently at every level, and a safe whistleblowing channel should exist.
markingPoints: Explains how senior behaviour signals whether rules matter
Leaders follow and brief the rules visibly
Clear, practical policies with reasons, developed with users
Regular training, support and open reporting of results
Consistent handling of breaches at all levels and a safe reporting channel

practical1.title: Draft a travel and expense claims policy and its operating procedure
practical1.brief: Your group is the finance team of a training organisation with centres in Kingston, Mandeville and Montego Bay. Staff travel between centres and the present rules are unwritten. Draft (1) a one- to two-page financial policy statement on travel and expense claims and (2) an operating procedure with numbered steps and a flowchart. Give each member a named role: policy lead (purpose, scope, definitions and policy statements), procedure writer (numbered steps, roles and time limits), flowchart designer, rates and limits officer (sets meal, mileage and hotel limits from figures the assessor gives, and works out two sample claims), and in a group of five a compliance officer (how the policy will be monitored and reviewed, with measures). The group presents the documents to the assessor as if to the finance committee, and each member explains their part for about 3 minutes. Photograph each stage and hand in once for the group.
materials: Scenario and rates sheet from the assessor
Computer with word processor and printer, or paper, rulers and pens
Flipchart and markers, sticky notes for building the flowchart
photos: The planning sheet with each member's name and role
The policy statement, showing purpose, scope, roles and version number
The operating procedure's numbered steps and the flowchart
The two sample claims worked out against the limits
The monitoring plan and a member presenting to the assessor
checklist: Carried out a named role and produced their own part of the evidence
Policy states purpose, scope, definitions, rules, roles and a review date
Procedure gives clear numbered steps, with who does each and the time limits
Flowchart matches the procedure, including approval and rejection paths
Sample claims are worked correctly against the stated limits
Monitoring plan names measures, methods and who reports to whom
Explained their part clearly and answered the assessor's questions
safety: Use made-up names and figures only; no real staff claims or bank details
Keep draft documents in the Centre's shared folder and delete copies from personal phones
Listen to each member's ideas and share the workload fairly
Take short breaks from the screen during the session

practical2.title: Test compliance with a financial procedure and report to the finance committee
practical2.brief: Your group is the internal review team of a hotel group. The assessor gives you the group's purchasing policy and procedure and a set of 20 sample purchase records (orders, receipts, invoices and approvals, all made up). Test each record against the procedure, record each breach on a test sheet, work out the compliance rate and find the causes. Then write a one-page monitoring report with findings and recommendations, and present it to a role-played finance committee (the assessor and one member). Give each member a named role: team lead (plans the test and checks the report), two testers (each tests 10 records and records the results), analyst (works out the compliance rate and groups the breaches by cause) and in a group of five a committee member who questions the team. Every member must speak in the committee meeting. Photograph each stage.
materials: Assessor's pack: purchasing policy and procedure and 20 sample records
Calculator or spreadsheet on a computer
photos: The completed test sheets for all 20 records
The analyst's working of the compliance rate and causes
The one-page monitoring report with recommendations
The action list agreed at the committee, with owners and dates
checklist: Carried out a named role and contributed to the written evidence
Tested records accurately against each step of the procedure
Compliance rate worked out correctly from the test results
Grouped breaches by cause (training, process, system, deliberate)
Recommendations are practical, proportionate and linked to the causes
Spoke clearly and professionally in the committee meeting
Agreed actions have owners, dates and a retest plan
safety: Treat the sample records as confidential and return every copy to the assessor
Report findings about processes, not about named individuals
Keep the committee role play respectful and constructive
Share the testing fairly so that no one is overloaded
